newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks dive, Nikkei down over 800 points.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks dive, Nikkei down over 800 points.

text.p: Japanese stocks fell sharply on Monday on fading hopes of any new economic policy initiatives in a keynote speech due to be delivered later in the day by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
The key Nikkei stock index shed more than 800 points as the market signalled its growing belief that the government would not offer any special steps to bolster confidence in the economy.

By early afternoon, the benchmark Nikkei 225 average had shed 760.73 points or 4.21 percent to stand at 17,329.31, after briefly sliding to 17,237.27, a drop of around 850 points. Brokers said that the slide was propelled by sales of shares in the steel and banking sectors.
Hashimoto was due to make his policy speech to the new session of parliament at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT).

The market had been hoping he might unveil or signal steps to shore up the sagging stock market, such as revisions to the government's budget for the fiscal year starting in April. But scepticism set in on Monday about the chances of the government rethinking its tight fiscal stance.

The Nikkei plunged more than 2,000 points in the first trading week of this year on worries that forthcoming tax increases could derail Japan's fragile economic recovery, but it recovered some ground last week.
